purpose: Store teacher actions separately from representations so MathBridge can explain how the same model can be used in more or less conceptually powerful ways.

moves.description_en: Make explicit links between concrete, pictorial, diagrammatic and symbolic forms rather than presenting them as separate activities.
moves.why_it_matters: Students can otherwise learn to operate each representation without understanding the invariant mathematical structure across them.
prompt_examples: What is the same in these two representations?
Where can you see this part of the equation in the diagram?
If I remove the counters, what information must the symbols preserve?

moves.description_en: Move from more explicit supports toward mental and symbolic reasoning when pupils can preserve the underlying structure without the support.
moves.why_it_matters: A representation should expose structure, not become a permanent procedure pupils cannot work without.
prompt_examples: Can you solve it without drawing every object?
What could you imagine instead of building it?
Which part of the model do you no longer need?

moves.description_en: Place two valid strategies or representations side by side and ask pupils to analyse efficiency, structure and generalisability.
moves.why_it_matters: Comparison can shift attention from obtaining an answer to understanding why methods work and when each is useful.
prompt_examples: Which method makes the place value easiest to see?
Why do both methods give the same result?
Which method would you choose for a larger number, and why?

moves.name_en: Vary One Feature at a Time
moves.name_cn: 有目的地改变一个特征
moves.description_en: Sequence examples so that selected features change while others remain stable, directing attention to mathematical structure and relationships.
moves.why_it_matters: Careful variation supports generalisation and helps pupils distinguish essential from non-essential features.
prompt_examples: What changed? What stayed the same?
Predict the next answer before calculating.
Which part of the representation must change if this number changes?

moves.description_en: Ask pupils to analyse quantities, relationships and known facts before carrying out a calculation.
moves.why_it_matters: This reduces indiscriminate procedure use and builds transfer between related problems.
prompt_examples: What do you notice before you calculate?
Which known fact can help?
What relationship is shown by the bar/array/number line?

moves.description_en: Require an explanation tied to mathematical relationships, not only a description of procedural steps.
moves.why_it_matters: A pupil can execute a procedure accurately without understanding the mathematical principle that justifies it.
prompt_examples: Why is regrouping allowed here?
Why does splitting the array not change the product?
Why are these fractions equivalent?

moves.name_cn: 先表征，再符号化或同步符号化
moves.description_en: Use objects, diagrams, actions or contexts to establish meaning, then connect them explicitly to mathematical symbols and equations.
moves.why_it_matters: Symbols are compressed representations; pupils need access to the quantities and relationships the symbols stand for.
prompt_examples: Show this equation with a diagram.
What does the 3 represent in this problem?
Write an equation that matches what you built.

moves.name_cn: 使用准确的数学语言句式
moves.description_en: Provide and rehearse concise sentence structures that express mathematical relationships accurately, then adapt them to new examples.
moves.why_it_matters: Language can make mathematical structure explicit and gives pupils a tool for explaining reasoning rather than relying on vague descriptions.
prompt_examples: 10 hundreds is equal to 1 thousand.
The whole is __ and the parts are __ and __.
I know __ because __.

moves.name_en: Use Errors and Misconceptions as Diagnostic Prompts
moves.name_cn: 利用错误与误解进行诊断
moves.description_en: Present or analyse incorrect representations and methods to identify which mathematical relationship has been misunderstood.
moves.why_it_matters: The location of an error often reveals whether the difficulty is conceptual, representational, linguistic or procedural.
prompt_examples: What has this pupil misunderstood?
Where does the diagram stop matching the equation?
How could we change one thing to make this correct?

moves.name_en: Move From Context to Mathematical Model
moves.name_cn: 从情境抽象到数学模型
moves.description_en: Identify the quantities and relationships in a real or word-problem context, express them with a representation, then operate symbolically.
moves.why_it_matters: This supports modelling and prevents key words from replacing analysis of mathematical structure.
prompt_examples: What quantities do we know?
How are the quantities related?
Which representation would make that relationship easiest to see?

ui_note: MathBridge should recommend a teaching move only when the selected representation, concept, grade/stage and evidence support it; these moves are not national stereotypes.
